claim_boundary: The registry records testable repository-supported causal hypotheses and controlled risks. A configured mechanism does not prove a customer or revenue effect; effect claims require owner-accepted metrics and controlled evidence.

patterns.title: Business truth can drift across customer-facing surfaces
patterns.root_rule: A value can become customer-facing before its provenance and owner-confirmation state are explicit.

evidence.note: The commercial-release checklist requires owner confirmation for hours, address, menu, contacts, assets, translations and consent.
The canonical profile stores publishable values but does not encode their owner-attestation state.
The machine-checked ledger binds each confirmed value to the canonical business profile by SHA-256 digest.
The machine-readable owner manifest binds all eleven confirmed values and digests to the production ledger.
The human-readable attestation record preserves provenance, scope, rollback and the claim boundary.

symptoms.description: A repository value and an owner-confirmed fact are not machine-distinguishable.
A guest can read a polished demo value as current café truth.
CI can validate format and consistency while remaining unable to reject an unconfirmed commercial fact.

intervention.new_rule: No owner-critical value is production-ready until its attestation is explicit and machine-checked.

actions.action: Maintain a versioned status ledger for every owner-critical field in the canonical business profile.
Fail closed when publication mode is production and any owner-critical value is not owner-confirmed.
Keep the release in explicit demo mode until the production truth gate can pass.

guardrails: Do not infer owner approval from the mere presence of a value in Git.
Do not weaken the production gate to make CI green.
Do not label demo data as commercially verified.
intervention.rollback: Keep publication_mode=demo and remove any production-readiness claim until owner confirmation is encoded.

patterns.falsification: Reject or downgrade this hypothesis if another canonical, machine-enforced owner-attestation source already covers every customer-facing business value.

patterns.title: An explained mechanism can be mistaken for a proven business effect
patterns.root_rule: A deterministic recommendation trace may be treated as evidence that the recommendation caused conversion or revenue.

evidence.note: The existing contract explicitly limits the trace to mechanism-only causality and requires controlled evidence for effect claims.

symptoms.description: The system can explain ranking, eligibility and observed transitions without estimating treatment effect.
A readable trace can still invite an unsupported claim about uplift, conversion or revenue.

intervention.new_rule: Mechanism evidence explains how; controlled outcome evidence is required to claim that it caused a business result.

actions.action: Preserve the mechanism-only claim level in every Smart Choice trace and report.
Require a predefined experiment, metric, guardrail and uncertainty statement before publishing an effect claim.
Treat effect-language without an experiment reference as an actionable review finding.

guardrails: Do not translate deterministic traceability into causal uplift.
Do not hide uncertainty or failed experiment guardrails.
intervention.rollback: Revert the statement to mechanism-only language and keep outcome changes as observations, not attributed effects.

patterns.falsification: Resolve this risk for a specific claim only when a correctly controlled design supports that exact claim and population.

patterns.title: Completion evidence can drift away from the exact branch head
patterns.root_rule: A change may be treated as complete using review or checks produced before the latest commit.

evidence.note: The PR contract says a new commit invalidates earlier review evidence, dispositions and the proof seal.
Repository instructions require checks, generated-file discipline and independent review after the latest commit.

symptoms.description: A green result can describe an earlier SHA rather than the code proposed for merge.
Maintainer intent, automated advice and independent approval can be conflated.

intervention.new_rule: Done means the complete evidence chain is bound to the exact current head and maintainer authority remains explicit.

actions.action: Bind CI, generated artifacts, dispositions and review evidence to the full current commit SHA.
Keep automated reviews advisory and require explicit human or accountable maintainer authorization.

guardrails: A new commit invalidates earlier readiness evidence.
An AI review never owns merge authority.
intervention.rollback: Revoke readiness for the stale SHA, rerun exact-head checks and obtain a new explicit decision.

patterns.falsification: Resolve the risk only when the release path cryptographically or procedurally rejects all stale-head evidence.
